firmographic.name: Braze
firmographic.company_description:
Braze is a publicly traded customer engagement platform (NASDAQ: BRZE) founded in 2011 and headquartered in New York, serving more than 2,600 brands across retail and eCommerce, financial services, travel and hospitality, media and entertainment, gaming, on-demand services, and QSR. The company's core proposition is unifying first-party customer data, AI-driven decisioning, and cross-channel message orchestration (email, mobile push, SMS/RCS, WhatsApp, web, in-app, and paid media) into a single platform used by brands to run personalized lifecycle marketing campaigns at scale, processing 4.5 trillion messages and 17.9 billion personalized AI decisions annually.

The platform is built on a composable architecture spanning the Braze Data Platform (zero-copy activation against Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure), BrazeAI (Decisioning Studio powered by OfferFit's multi-agent reinforcement learning, Agent Console, Operator, and Creative Studio with Figma/Canva), Canvas journey orchestration, and Reporting & Analytics. Braze monetizes through tiered annual and multi-year subscriptions (Go, Select, Pro, Enterprise) priced on Monthly Active Users, supplemented by a usage-based Action Credits model for message volume and AI products, and by professional services. Distribution combines direct enterprise field sales, inside sales, a self-service PLG motion for startups, and the 2,100+ partner Braze Alloys network.

Go-to-market spans enterprise, mid-market, and SMB tiers globally with offices in New York, London, Austin, Sydney, and regional operations in the Philippines and Japan. The company holds three consecutive years as a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Multichannel Marketing Hubs, a 2026 Forrester Wave Leader for Email Marketing Service Providers, and a 110% dollar-based net retention rate. Recent strategic emphasis has shifted toward AI monetization via the OfferFit integration, agentic AI tools, a $100M share repurchase program announced March 2026, and operational scaling ahead of a targeted FY2029 profitability milestone.

recent_move.description: Acquired OfferFit Inc. for approximately $325 million and integrated its multi-agent reinforcement learning engine into the BrazeAI Decisioning Studio to strengthen 1:1 personalization capabilities.

Launched BrazeAI Operator (Beta), BrazeAI Agent Console, and Braze Creative Studio with Figma/Canva integrations, and brought EU hosting of BrazeAI Decisioning Studio to Google Cloud for GDPR compliance.
Authorized the company's first $100 million share repurchase program (including a $50 million accelerated buyback) to return capital and signal management confidence in valuation.

Announced CFO Isabelle Winkles' departure with CAO Pankaj Malik as Interim CFO and appointed former Fastly/NYT CIO Nick Rockwell as Chief Information Officer effective June 1, 2026; General Counsel Susan Wiseman also plans to retire by June 30, 2026.
Formed a deep partnership with Wunderkind to embed identity resolution and high-intent behavioral triggers directly into Braze journeys, with brands reporting up to 8x lift in triggered revenue.
Acquired North Star, its exclusive ANZ reseller, for $28 million to convert it into a wholly owned Braze Australia subsidiary, converting channel economics into direct regional revenue.
Braze completed its acquisition of North Star, its exclusive reseller in Australia and New Zealand, and now operates as Braze Australia to enhance regional customer service and market presence.

expansion_highlight.description: Braze launched a Southeast Asia-focused 'Grow with Braze Asia' conference in Manila in June 2026 and previously established the Braze Australia subsidiary after acquiring North Star, indicating continued APAC investment beyond the legacy US/UK footprint.

General availability of BrazeAI Operator (Beta), BrazeAI Agent Console, and Braze Creative Studio in April 2026 extends the product surface from decisioning into autonomous agent execution and creative operations, materially expanding addressable wallet share within existing accounts.

Introduction of the Action Credits usage-based pricing model for AI products and message volume, layered on top of the Go/Select/Pro/Enterprise subscription tiers, broadens monetization flexibility and creates a variable revenue stream alongside subscriptions.

Appointment of Nick Rockwell (former Fastly and NYT CIO) as Chief Information Officer with a remit over AI transformation, data governance, and enterprise data flows points to organizational buildout for enterprise-scale AI deployments and compliance.

OfferFit acquisition ($325M) and the Wunderkind identity-resolution partnership, alongside the Databricks CustomerLake launch partnership, extend the AI and ecosystem surface area through inorganic and cooperative moves rather than purely internal R&D.

Braze Alloys grew to 2,100+ partners with 140–180+ turnkey integrations including co-marketing awards in Japan and regional partners like Dentsu Digital, signaling active ecosystem buildout as a distribution and product-extension lever.
